subject: Rust client hardware feasibility for NORA

method.scope: Focused primary documentation/source review; Exa discovery/fetch and GitHub connector source inspection. No implementation, compile, model download or benchmark.
method.meaning: URLs or source files inspected, not independent experiments or exhaustive full-paper audits. Search snippets can be stale; direct file inspection supersedes conflicting snippets.
method.comparison: Architectural inference, no measured NORA Rust/Python delta; proposed ADR remains unaccepted.

sources.title: Ownership
sources.supports: Ownership-based memory management.
sources.caveats: No NORA RAM or speed benchmark; Rust does not eliminate native/model allocation.

sources.title: Reference cycles and memory leaks
sources.supports: Safe Rust can still leak memory via reference cycles.
sources.caveats: Not a claim that all retained memory is a leak.

sources.title: Unsafe Rust
sources.supports: Unsafe/FFI boundaries require contracts beyond safe caller code.
sources.caveats: Memory safety does not implement agent authorization or prompt-injection defense.

sources.title: whisper.cpp README
sources.supports: C/C++ inference and quantization; host language differs from engine.
sources.caveats: Fetched README excerpt; generic model memory table is not turbo-specific NORA peak RAM.

sources.title: whisper-rs API
sources.supports: Rust API/bindings for whisper.cpp.
sources.caveats: Not a pure-Rust reimplementation or hardware-performance proof.

sources.title: ort introduction
sources.supports: Rust binding for ONNX Runtime and compatible backends.
sources.caveats: Maintainer production-ready language is not independent audit; version/site snapshots can differ.

sources.title: ONNX Runtime memory tuning
sources.supports: Shared allocators and allocator tuning affect memory.
sources.caveats: Benefits depend on session/provider/lifecycle; no quantified NORA savings.

sources.title: ONNX Runtime C API
sources.supports: Session APIs, shared threadpools and allocator controls.
sources.caveats: Options must actually be supported/exposed in chosen Rust wrapper; not automatic.

sources.title: ONNX Runtime device tensors
sources.supports: Device I/O/copy control, with comparable optimization opportunities in Python API.
sources.caveats: Changing host language alone is not proof of reduced GPU memory or transfer count.

sources.title: ONNX Runtime threading
sources.supports: Threadpool sizing and spinning affect CPU utilization.
sources.caveats: Throughput/latency/power trade-offs need workload-specific tests.

sources.title: Tauri process model
sources.supports: Rust core and separate WebView processes; Windows uses WebView2.
sources.caveats: Rust frontend/WASM does not remove browser engine; hidden window does not establish process reclamation.

sources.title: egui/eframe README
sources.supports: Native and web Rust GUI option.
sources.caveats: No evidence native UI always uses less memory; rendering/accessibility trade-offs remain.

sources.title: VieNeu-TTS English README
sources.supports: CPU fp32 default, INT8/VNNI caveat, author CPU cold-load14-19seconds in specified benchmark.
sources.caveats: Author hardware/configuration differs from NORA; not NORA timing or guaranteed general result.

sources.title: VieNeu-TTS dependencies
sources.supports: Torch-free CPU stack and native-backed dependencies; manifest also includes Web UI packages.
sources.caveats: Installed package size is not resident RAM; license/data/model rights require separate review.

sources.title: VieNeu-TTS ONNX CPU engine
sources.supports: Multiple CPU ONNX sessions, NumPy/control sampling, KV/streaming state, thread limits and spinning configuration.
sources.caveats: Source inspection only, not executed/profiled; no completed Rust port or formal quality equivalence.

sources.title: sea-g2p README
sources.supports: Rust core and C ABI for non-Python hosts.
sources.caveats: Pin ABI/dictionary/assets/license; not proof complete VieNeu pipeline has a stable Rust SDK.

sources.title: Hugging Face tokenizers README
sources.supports: Rust tokenizer core/crate with language bindings and optional features.
sources.caveats: Tokenizer availability alone does not establish full TTS parity.

sources.title: Silero VAD README
sources.supports: ONNX deployment and upstream Rust examples; sample-rate constraints.
sources.caveats: No new benchmark; initial Exa fetch to silero-ai timed out, verified through GitHub snakers4 source instead.

sources.title: Rig README
sources.supports: Rust LLM/agent components exist.
sources.caveats: Do not import broad coding tools/plugins by default; not a drop-in NORA durable/security runtime.

sources.title: Candle README
sources.supports: Rust ML framework lists Whisper and hardware backends.
sources.caveats: Does not prove equivalent VieNeu/quantization/operator support or better NORA performance.

sources.title: Cargo profiles
sources.supports: Release optimization, LTO and symbol stripping controls.
sources.caveats: Flags affect application code/binary; no model-weight reduction or automatic runtime win.

sources.title: rustc codegen options
sources.reading_scope: Exa codegen extract requested100000characters; target-cpu section inspected
sources.supports: target-cpu=native targets host processor; CPU/feature flags affect compatibility.
sources.caveats: Portable product builds need explicit compatibility/dispatch tests; not a universal compiler tuning recipe.

sources.title: VieNeu-TTS Vietnamese README (direct source)
sources.supports: Direct current file agrees with English fp32 default; older search snippet said int8.
sources.caveats: Use direct pinned source/version; do not allege current doc mismatch based on stale search snippets.
